record.summary: Pooja Singh, 29, reports that her husband Vikas has been physically abusive for two years. Tonight, after an argument about money, he threw a glass at her, grabbed her throat, and threatened to kill her if she leaves. He is now asleep in the next room. Pooja is in the bathroom with her phone, her 4‑year‑old daughter is sleeping in the bedroom, and she has no personal money because Vikas controls their bank account. She fears calling the police because Vikas claimed he has friends in the police. She seeks immediate guidance on how to ensure her safety and that of her daughter, preserve evidence, and understand custody implications.
record.goal: To obtain immediate safety for herself and her daughter, learn how to remove her husband from the house, preserve evidence, and address custody concerns while planning to leave the abusive environment.
questions: Do you have any safe place (relative's house, friend’s home, shelter) you can go to right now?
Do you have any identification documents (Aadhaar, PAN, passport) with you that could help you access services or shelter?
Have you ever filed a police complaint or obtained a protection order against Vikas before?
Can you note the approximate time (e.g., 10 pm, around midnight) when the assault occurred tonight?
Would you be able to seek immediate medical attention for your injuries, or have you already done so?
evidence: Visible redness and early bruising on neck and a cut on forearm from tonight's incident; photos can be taken with phone date‑time stamp.
Messages from Vikas over the past year containing threats.
Voice note from Vikas threatening to take the child away.
Hospital record from 14 months ago documenting a wrist injury.
Possible police call record by a neighbor regarding prior shouting.
Friend Rekha knows about the abuse and is willing to speak up.

evidence_plan.heading: Evidence plan
prompts: Which part of the timeline needs independent support?
What already shows that event, and who may lawfully hold another record?

suggestions.title: Movement and viewing position
suggestions.look_for: Record the last direction you personally saw, nearby landmarks, and anything that limited your view. Separate what you saw from what others reported.
suggestions.why: It helps police identify which witnesses or time windows may be relevant.
suggestions.action: Write down your recollection while it is fresh. Do not follow or confront anyone.

suggestions.title: Original records and an evidence log
suggestions.look_for: Keep records you lawfully have, with their surrounding context. For each item note the related event, who provided it, when you received it, and any transfer.
suggestions.why: The log distinguishes what you observed from what someone later told you and makes it easier to check the source.
suggestions.action: Keep an unchanged original and label working copies. Avoid editing originals, guessing gaps, or sharing evidence publicly.
